Let the line \(y=2x\) have angle \(\theta\), so \(\tan\theta=2\). Then
\[
\cos 2\theta=\frac{1-4}{1+4}=-\frac35,\qquad \sin 2\theta=\frac{4}{5}.
\]
Reflection over this line maps original coordinates \((X,Y)\) to new coordinates \((x,y)\) by
\[
\begin{pmatrix}X\\Y\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
-\frac35 & \frac45\\[2mm]
\frac45 & \frac35
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
X=\frac{-3x+4y}{5},\qquad Y=\frac{4x+3y}{5}.
\]
Since \(XY=1\),
\[
\left(\frac{-3x+4y}{5}\right)\left(\frac{4x+3y}{5}\right)=1.
\]
So
\[
(-3x+4y)(4x+3y)=25
\]
\[
-12x^2+7xy+12y^2=25.
\]
Multiplying by \(-1\):
\[
12x^2-7xy-12y^2+25=0.
\]
Thus \(b=-7\), \(c=-12\), so
\[
bc=(-7)(-12)=84.
\]
\[
\boxed{84}
\]
